units.function: Unit and embedded-Postgres tests for normalizing OpenClaw/Hermes Gateway invitation defaults, deriving authentication material, enforcing transport diagnostics and replacing a literal Hermes API key with a persisted Company SecretRef.
units.dependencyDirection: Vendor adapter type, inbound headers, invite defaults and deployment settings enter access-route normalizers; OpenClaw device keys may be generated in-process, Hermes URLs are rewritten/validated, and persistence preparation writes through Company secret services/tables before a join request stores the resulting adapter payload.
units.keyDataModels: Gateway URL/API base/Paperclip URL, authorization/x-openclaw-token/apiKey, disableDeviceAuth/devicePrivateKeyPem, dangerous insecure-HTTP flag, fatalErrors/diagnostic code-level-message-hint, Company secret/provider/version records and secret_ref secretId/version latest.
units.lifecycle: Non-gateway defaults pass through. OpenClaw tokens are unwrapped or derived from inbound/Authorization headers and device authentication generates a persistent private key unless disabled. Hermes rejects remote HTTP unless explicitly overridden and maps dashboard/chat roots to its API path. Before persistence, a literal Hermes API key becomes a Company secret and the join request stores a SecretRef rather than plaintext.
units.testAssessment: Useful tests cover token input variants, device-auth key generation, explicit unsafe transport override, stable diagnostics, vendor URL correction and real-database proof that one literal Hermes key is absent from the join payload. Missing are OpenClaw token/private-key secretization, immutable secret version binding, log/error/activity redaction, header allowlisting, URL SSRF/egress policy, secret ownership/expiry/rotation/revocation, transaction rollback/orphan cleanup, concurrent deduplication, key file permissions/HSM or external vault adapters, approver visibility and proof that no plaintext appears in WAL/backups/telemetry.
units.designRationale: Make external gateway onboarding forgiving enough to normalize common configurations while preventing accidental remote cleartext and moving long-lived credentials out of ordinary Agent configuration JSON.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Connector onboarding that normalizes vendor configuration without leaking secrets, works with cloud or enterprise vaults and binds approval to the exact runtime credential/version and network policy.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the validate-normalize-diagnose-persist sequence, explicit unsafe transport diagnostic and secret-handle replacement. Generalize it behind Connector manifests and SecretPort; validate egress separately, allow only declared fields, store immutable SecretVersion IDs in approved ConnectorBinding revisions, rotate through a new binding/approval, generate device private keys inside the execution node and return only public-key attestation to the control plane.
units.responsibilityConflict: The persisted Hermes reference uses version latest, so a later secret rotation changes execution credentials without changing or reapproving the join payload. Raw OpenClaw tokens are duplicated across Authorization and x-openclaw-token, and a device private key is generated in control-plane normalization with no proven vault treatment. The unsafe HTTP flag is caller data rather than a qualified-human/data-owner approval bound to an exact endpoint.
